title: Finance, Growth and Decay: Depreciation and Nominal and Effective Rates
seo_title: Grade 11 Finance, Growth and Decay Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Use simple and compound decay formulae A = P(1 − in) and A = P(1 − i)ⁿ to solve problems (including straight line depreciation and depreciation on a reducing balance); the effect of different periods of compound growth and decay, including nominal and effective interest rates.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 11 finance worksheets: straight-line and reducing-balance depreciation, nominal and effective interest rates and compound interest. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: A = P(1 − i)ⁿ for reducing balance.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Straight-line (simple) depreciation: A = P(1 − in). Reducing-balance: A = P(1 − i)ⁿ.
  • Compound interest with m periods a year: A = P(1 + im)mn.
  • Effective rate: 1 + ieff = (1 + inomm)m.
  • Draw a timeline when the rate or payments change.

Examples

Example

12% p.a. compounded monthly

(1 + 0,01)¹² − 1

Answer: 12,68% effective

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The methodReducing balance uses a power.
Nominal or effectiveCompounded monthly gives more than the nominal rate.
mnUse the number of periods, not years.

faq.a: Use simple and compound decay formulae for depreciation, and calculate the effects of different periods of compounding growth and decay, including effective and nominal interest rates.

faq.q: Which method loses value faster at first?
faq.a: Straight-line, for the same rate after the first year.
Yes, when interest compounds more than once a year.
